title: Health Assessments
need: I want a thorough, honest picture of my health
summary: A physician-led morning built around your history rather than a fixed checklist, followed by a written report and a second conversation three months later.
intro: A good assessment is not the largest possible set of tests. It is the right tests for your age, family history and concerns, interpreted by a doctor who has spent time with you. We leave out investigations that tend to find harmless abnormalities and lead to more tests, and we explain why.
image_alt: Blood pressure being taken by hand with a cuff and dial
for_whom: Adults over 35 who haven't had a thorough review in several years
People with a family history of heart disease, diabetes or certain cancers
Anyone who wants a baseline before a change: a new role, a training goal, a decade birthday

includes.title: An hour with a physician
includes.detail: History, examination, and a conversation about what is actually on your mind, before any tests are chosen.

includes.title: Blood and urine tests
includes.detail: Chosen for you. Typically a cholesterol profile, HbA1c, kidney and liver function, full blood count, thyroid and ferritin, with others where your history suggests them.

includes.title: Heart and circulation
includes.detail: A resting ECG, and blood pressure measured properly: seated, repeated and, where needed, over 24 hours at home.

includes.title: Strength and fitness
includes.detail: Grip strength, a simple walking or step test, and a frank conversation about activity you would genuinely keep up.

includes.title: Screening, where evidence supports it
includes.detail: Cervical, bowel or skin checks according to age and risk, and a clear explanation of the screening we would not recommend for you.

includes.title: A written report
includes.detail: In plain English within five working days: each result explained, and a short list of priorities.

process.detail: A coordinator takes your history in outline and confirms any fasting instructions.
Arrive at 8:30. Bloods first, then breakfast in the garden room, then your physician and the remaining tests.
Within a week, in person or by video, with your report in hand.
What changed, what didn't, and what comes next.

fees.note: Ages 40 and over. Adds cardiac and body-composition tests.
Only when your history or results point to it.

faqs.q: Will you include a whole-body scan?
faqs.a: Not routinely. In people without symptoms, whole-body scanning often finds incidental abnormalities that prove harmless but lead to further tests and worry. If your history suggests a specific scan is worthwhile, we will recommend it and explain why.
Usually for eight to ten hours beforehand; water is fine. Your coordinator confirms this for your particular tests.

faqs.q: Can my partner come on the same day?
faqs.a: Yes. Couples often book the same morning with different physicians, and share breakfast in between.
